snippets.title: Remove Duplicates overwrites a kept value
snippets.code:
def remove_duplicates(nums):
    """Remove duplicates from a sorted list in place.

    Returns the number of unique values; they end up at the front of nums.
    """
    if not nums:
        return 0
    write = 1
    for read in range(1, len(nums)):
        if nums[read] != nums[write]:
            nums[write] = nums[read]
            write += 1
    return write


nums = [1, 2, 2, 3]
k = remove_duplicates(nums)
print(k, nums[:k])
snippets.bug: The new value is compared with nums[write], the slot about to be overwritten, instead of the last kept value nums[write - 1]. A kept 2 gets replaced by the 3.
snippets.fixedCode:
def remove_duplicates(nums):
    """Remove duplicates from a sorted list in place.

    Returns the number of unique values; they end up at the front of nums.
    """
    if not nums:
        return 0
    write = 1
    for read in range(1, len(nums)):
        if nums[read] != nums[write - 1]:
            nums[write] = nums[read]
            write += 1
    return write


nums = [1, 2, 2, 3]
k = remove_duplicates(nums)
print(k, nums[:k])
snippets.explanation: `write` points at the next free slot, so the last kept value is nums[write - 1]. Compare against that. The pass is O(n) time, O(1) space.

snippets.title: Rotate Image does nothing useful
snippets.bug: The inner loop visits every pair twice, so each swap is undone by its mirror and the matrix is never transposed. Only the row reversal takes effect.
snippets.explanation: Swap only the cells above the diagonal: j runs over range(i + 1, n). Each pair is then swapped exactly once. Time O(n²), space O(1).

snippets.title: Product of Array Except Self wrong suffix
snippets.code:
def product_except_self(nums):
    """out[i] = product of every element except nums[i], without division."""
    n = len(nums)
    out = [1] * n

    prefix = 1
    for i in range(n):
        out[i] = prefix
        prefix *= nums[i]

    suffix = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= out[i]
    return out


print(product_except_self([1, 2, 3, 4]))
snippets.bug: The running suffix is multiplied by out[i], which already holds a prefix product, instead of by the original value nums[i].
snippets.fixedCode:
def product_except_self(nums):
    """out[i] = product of every element except nums[i], without division."""
    n = len(nums)
    out = [1] * n

    prefix = 1
    for i in range(n):
        out[i] = prefix
        prefix *= nums[i]

    suffix = 1
    for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= nums[i]
    return out


print(product_except_self([1, 2, 3, 4]))
snippets.explanation: `suffix` must be the product of the original elements to the right, so multiply it by nums[i]. After the fix the function is O(n) time and O(1) extra space (the output excluded).

snippets.title: Longest unique substring moves left backwards
snippets.code:
def longest_unique(s):
    """Length of the longest substring without repeating characters."""
    last = {}  # char -> index of its latest occurrence
    left = 0
    best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch in last:
            left = last[ch] + 1
        last[ch] = right
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best


def check(s):
    result = longest_unique(s)
    assert 0 <= result <= len(s)
    return result


print(check("abba"))
snippets.bug: `left` is set to just after the previous occurrence even when that occurrence is already outside the window, so the window can move backwards (for "abba" it jumps from 2 back to 1).
snippets.fixedCode:
def longest_unique(s):
    """Length of the longest substring without repeating characters."""
    last = {}  # char -> index of its latest occurrence
    left = 0
    best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch in last:
            left = max(left, last[ch] + 1)
        last[ch] = right
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best


def check(s):
    result = longest_unique(s)
    assert 0 <= result <= len(s)
    return result


print(check("abba"))
snippets.explanation: The left edge must never decrease: use `left = max(left, last[ch] + 1)`. This is still O(n) time and O(min(n, alphabet)) space.

snippets.title: Visits leak between sessions
snippets.code:
def add_visit(page, visits=[]):
    visits.append(page)
    return visits


def build_session(pages):
    session = add_visit(pages[0])
    for page in pages[1:]:
        add_visit(page, session)
    return session


first = build_session(["home", "docs"])
second = build_session(["pricing"])
print(len(first), len(second))
snippets.bug: The default list `[]` is created once, when the function is defined, so every call that omits `visits` appends to the same list.
snippets.explanation: Use `visits=None` and create the list inside the function. Default values are evaluated once at definition time, so a mutable default is shared by all calls.

snippets.title: Subarray Sum Equals K misses prefixes
snippets.code:
def subarray_sum(nums, k):
    """Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k."""
    counts = {}  # prefix sum -> how many times it has occurred
    total = 0
    result = 0
    for x in nums:
        total += x
        result += counts.get(total - k, 0)
        counts[total] = counts.get(total, 0) + 1
    return result


def check(nums, k):
    result = subarray_sum(nums, k)
    assert result >= 0
    return result


print(check([1, 2, 3], 3))
snippets.bug: The map does not start with the empty prefix, so subarrays that begin at index 0 (like [1, 2]) are never counted.
snippets.fix: counts = {0: 1}  # the empty prefix has sum 0
snippets.fixedCode:
def subarray_sum(nums, k):
    """Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k."""
    counts = {0: 1}  # the empty prefix has sum 0
    total = 0
    result = 0
    for x in nums:
        total += x
        result += counts.get(total - k, 0)
        counts[total] = counts.get(total, 0) + 1
    return result


def check(nums, k):
    result = subarray_sum(nums, k)
    assert result >= 0
    return result


print(check([1, 2, 3], 3))
snippets.explanation: Seed the map with {0: 1}: a prefix whose own sum equals k pairs with the empty prefix. The scan is O(n) time and O(n) space.

snippets.title: Valid Palindrome is case sensitive
snippets.bug: Characters are compared as they are, so 'A' and 'a' differ and a valid palindrome is rejected.
snippets.explanation: Normalize case before comparing: `s[left].lower() != s[right].lower()`. The two-pointer scan is O(n) time and O(1) space.

snippets.title: Group Anagrams cannot hash the key
snippets.bug: `sorted(word)` returns a list, and a list is unhashable, so using it as a dict key raises TypeError.
snippets.explanation: Dict keys must be hashable. Convert the sorted letters to a tuple (or join them into a string). The grouping then costs O(n · k log k) time and O(n · k) space.

snippets.title: Top K Frequent shares one bucket
snippets.bug: `[[]] * n` makes n references to ONE list, so every value lands in every bucket and the order is by first appearance, not by frequency.
snippets.explanation: List multiplication copies references, not lists. A comprehension creates a fresh list per bucket. The fixed version is O(n) time and space.

snippets.title: Longest Consecutive is one short
snippets.code:
def longest_consecutive(nums):
    """Length of the longest run of consecutive integers."""
    present = set(nums)
    best = 0
    for x in present:
        if x - 1 in present:
            continue  # x is not the start of a run
        end = x
        while end + 1 in present:
            end += 1
        best = max(best, end - x)
    return best


def check(nums):
    result = longest_consecutive(nums)
    assert result <= len(set(nums))
    return result


print(check([100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]))
snippets.bug: The run from x to end contains end - x + 1 numbers; the code stores the distance between them, which is one less.
snippets.fixedCode:
def longest_consecutive(nums):
    """Length of the longest run of consecutive integers."""
    present = set(nums)
    best = 0
    for x in present:
        if x - 1 in present:
            continue  # x is not the start of a run
        end = x
        while end + 1 in present:
            end += 1
        best = max(best, end - x + 1)
    return best


def check(nums):
    result = longest_consecutive(nums)
    assert result <= len(set(nums))
    return result


print(check([100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]))
snippets.explanation: A run of the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 has length 4 but end - x = 3. Counting numbers, not gaps, fixes the off-by-one. The algorithm is O(n): each run is walked once, from its start.

snippets.title: Range Sum drops the last element
snippets.bug: pre[i] is the sum of the first i numbers, so a range that includes `right` ends at pre[right + 1]. The code leaves the last element out.
snippets.explanation: Because pre has a leading 0, pre[j + 1] - pre[i] is the sum of nums[i..j]. Each query is O(1); building pre is O(n).

snippets.title: Contiguous Array misses a prefix
snippets.code:
def find_max_length(nums):
    """Longest subarray of 0s and 1s with equally many of each."""
    first_seen = {}  # running balance -> first index where it occurred
    balance = 0
    best = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        balance += 1 if x == 1 else -1
        if balance in first_seen:
            best = max(best, i - first_seen[balance])
        else:
            first_seen[balance] = i
    return best


def check(nums):
    result = find_max_length(nums)
    assert result % 2 == 0
    return result


print(check([0, 0, 1, 1]))
snippets.bug: The map does not know that a balance of 0 existed before index 0, so a balanced slice that starts at the first element is never found.
snippets.fix: first_seen = {0: -1}  # running balance -> first index where it occurred
snippets.fixedCode:
def find_max_length(nums):
    """Longest subarray of 0s and 1s with equally many of each."""
    first_seen = {0: -1}  # running balance -> first index where it occurred
    balance = 0
    best = 0
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        balance += 1 if x == 1 else -1
        if balance in first_seen:
            best = max(best, i - first_seen[balance])
        else:
            first_seen[balance] = i
    return best


def check(nums):
    result = find_max_length(nums)
    assert result % 2 == 0
    return result


print(check([0, 0, 1, 1]))
snippets.explanation: Seed the map with {0: -1}: the empty prefix ends at index -1. Then a balanced slice from index 0 to i has length i - (-1) = i + 1. O(n) time, O(n) space.

snippets.title: Sudoku box index is wrong
snippets.code:
def is_valid_sudoku(board):
    """True if no digit repeats in a row, column or 3x3 box ('.' = empty)."""
    rows = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    cols = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    boxes = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    for r in range(9):
        for c in range(9):
            d = board[r][c]
            if d == ".":
                continue
            b = (r // 3) * 3 + c % 3
            if d in rows[r] or d in cols[c] or d in boxes[b]:
                return False
            rows[r].add(d)
            cols[c].add(d)
            boxes[b].add(d)
    return True


board = [["."] * 9 for _ in range(9)]
board[0][0] = "5"
board[1][3] = "5"  # different row, column and box
print(is_valid_sudoku(board))
snippets.bug: The box number uses `c % 3` instead of `c // 3`, so cells in different boxes share an id (cells (0, 0) and (1, 3) both map to box 0) and a valid board is rejected.
snippets.fixedCode:
def is_valid_sudoku(board):
    """True if no digit repeats in a row, column or 3x3 box ('.' = empty)."""
    rows = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    cols = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    boxes = [set() for _ in range(9)]
    for r in range(9):
        for c in range(9):
            d = board[r][c]
            if d == ".":
                continue
            b = (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3
            if d in rows[r] or d in cols[c] or d in boxes[b]:
                return False
            rows[r].add(d)
            cols[c].add(d)
            boxes[b].add(d)
    return True


board = [["."] * 9 for _ in range(9)]
board[0][0] = "5"
board[1][3] = "5"  # different row, column and box
print(is_valid_sudoku(board))
snippets.explanation: The 3x3 box of a cell is (row // 3, col // 3), flattened as (r // 3) * 3 + c // 3. The modulo gives the position inside a box, not the box. One pass over 81 cells, O(1) for a fixed size.

snippets.title: First Missing Positive stops too early
snippets.bug: When every slot 1..n holds its own number, the first missing positive is n + 1, not n.
snippets.explanation: The answer always lies in 1..n + 1. If the scan finds no mismatch, 1..n are all present, so the answer is n + 1. The swapping is O(n) time overall and the function uses O(1) extra space.

snippets.title: Multipliers all use the last factor
snippets.bug: Each lambda looks up `f` when it is CALLED, by which time the loop has finished and f is the last factor, so all three functions multiply by 3.
snippets.fix: return [lambda x, f=f: x * f for f in factors]
snippets.explanation: Closures capture variables, not values (late binding). A default argument `f=f` freezes the current value when the lambda is created; `functools.partial` also works.

snippets.title: Two Sum II reuses one element
snippets.bug: With `<=` the loop also runs when left == right, so a single element can be added to itself: for [1, 2, 4] and target 4 it reports the pair 1 and 1 (2 + 2).
snippets.explanation: A pair needs two different positions, so the loop must stop when the pointers meet. Fixed, the scan is O(n) time and O(1) space.

snippets.title: Longest unique substring shrinks only once
snippets.code:
def longest_unique(s):
    """Length of the longest substring with no repeated character."""
    seen = set()
    left = best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch in seen:
            seen.remove(s[left])
            left += 1
        seen.add(ch)
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best


def check(s):
    result = longest_unique(s)
    assert result <= len(s)
    return result


print(check("abba"))
snippets.bug: `if` removes one character from the left and moves on, even if the repeated letter is still inside the window, so the window keeps a duplicate and the length is over-counted (3 instead of 2 for "abba").
snippets.fixedCode:
def longest_unique(s):
    """Length of the longest substring with no repeated character."""
    seen = set()
    left = best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        while ch in seen:
            seen.remove(s[left])
            left += 1
        seen.add(ch)
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best


def check(s):
    result = longest_unique(s)
    assert result <= len(s)
    return result


print(check("abba"))
snippets.explanation: The window must shrink until it is valid again, which needs a `while`. Left only moves forward, so the total work is still O(n) time, O(min(n, alphabet)) space.

snippets.title: Container With Most Water moves the taller wall
snippets.code:
def max_area(height):
    """Largest amount of water two vertical lines can hold."""
    left, right = 0, len(height) - 1
    best = 0
    while left < right:
        width = right - left
        best = max(best, width * min(height[left], height[right]))
        if height[left] > height[right]:
            left += 1
        else:
            right -= 1
    return best


def check(height):
    result = max_area(height)
    assert result >= 0
    return result


print(check([1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7]))
snippets.bug: The pointer on the TALLER wall is moved. The area is limited by the shorter wall, so moving the taller one can never help, and the good pairs are skipped (the code returns 8 instead of 49).
snippets.fixedCode:
def max_area(height):
    """Largest amount of water two vertical lines can hold."""
    left, right = 0, len(height) - 1
    best = 0
    while left < right:
        width = right - left
        best = max(best, width * min(height[left], height[right]))
        if height[left] < height[right]:
            left += 1
        else:
            right -= 1
    return best


def check(height):
    result = max_area(height)
    assert result >= 0
    return result


print(check([1, 8, 6, 2, 5, 4, 8, 3, 7]))
snippets.explanation: Always move the shorter wall: any pair that keeps it can only be narrower with the same or lower height. That makes the O(n) scan correct, with O(1) space.

snippets.title: 3Sum repeats a triple
snippets.bug: After recording a triple the code steps `left` by one only. An equal value right next to it forms the identical triple again, so [-2, 0, 2] is reported twice.
snippets.explanation: In sorted order duplicates are adjacent, so skip past every copy of the second number after a hit. The scan stays O(n²) time overall, O(1) extra space besides the output.

snippets.title: Minimum Size Subarray returns infinity
snippets.bug: When no window ever reaches the target, `best` is still the starting value infinity and that is returned instead of 0.
snippets.fix: return 0 if best == float("inf") else best
snippets.explanation: A search that can find nothing needs an explicit 'not found' result. The window itself is correct: O(n) time, O(1) space.

snippets.title: Trapping Rain Water forgets the last bar
snippets.bug: right_max is filled from the right, but its last cell is never seeded, so it stays 0 and corrupts every value computed from it.
snippets.explanation: A running maximum needs a starting value: the last bar is its own right maximum (just as left_max[0] is seeded). The arrays version is O(n) time and O(n) space.

snippets.title: Permutation in String drops the wrong letter
snippets.bug: The letter leaving the window is s2[i - len(s1)], but the code removes s2[i - len(s1) - 1], one position too far back, so the counts describe the wrong substring (here it wrongly reports that "eidboaoo" contains a permutation of "ab").
snippets.explanation: Once the window has len(s1) letters, adding index i must drop index i - len(s1). An off-by-one here corrupts every later window. O(n) time, O(1) space for 26 letters.

snippets.title: Summary reads a spent generator
snippets.bug: `sq` is a generator and `sum(sq)` has already consumed it, so `max(sq)` sees an empty sequence and raises ValueError.
snippets.actual: ERROR: ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty
snippets.explanation: A generator can be traversed once. Call the generator function again, or store the values in a list (O(n) space) if you need several passes.

snippets.title: Binary search starts one past the end
snippets.bug: The loop treats [lo, hi] as a closed range of valid indices, but hi starts at len(nums), one past the last index, so mid can reach len(nums) and nums[mid] raises IndexError.
snippets.actual: ERROR: IndexError: list index out of range
snippets.explanation: With `while lo <= hi` both ends must be valid positions: hi = len(nums) - 1. (The half-open form uses hi = len(nums) with `while lo < hi`.) Search is O(log n) time, O(1) space.

snippets.title: Lower bound finds the upper bound
snippets.bug: `<=` skips over elements equal to x, so the search ends after the last x (the upper bound, 4) instead of at the first one (1).
snippets.explanation: Lower bound: move right only while a[mid] < x. Upper bound: while a[mid] <= x. The difference is one character and the whole answer. Both run in O(log n).

snippets.title: Merge sort is not stable
snippets.bug: On equal keys the strict `<` falls to the else branch and takes the RIGHT item first, reversing the order of equal elements ("b" before "a").
snippets.explanation: Take the left item on ties (`<=`) to keep equal elements in their original order. That is the only difference between a stable and an unstable merge. O(n log n) time, O(n) space.

snippets.title: Quickselect is off by one
snippets.bug: k counts from 1, but the code compares it with `<`, so the boundaries between `less`, `equal` and `more` are shifted by one position and the next larger value is returned.
snippets.explanation: For a 1-based k the k-th smallest lies in `less` when k <= len(less), is the pivot when k <= len(less) + len(equal), and otherwise lies in `more`. Average O(n) time.

snippets.title: Rotated search fails on two elements
snippets.bug: When lo == mid (a range of one or two items) `nums[lo] < nums[mid]` is False even though the left 'half' is sorted, so the code searches the wrong side and returns -1.
snippets.explanation: mid is rounded down, so it can equal lo; a one-element left half is sorted. Use `<=` to treat it as the sorted half. O(log n) time, O(1) space.

snippets.title: Eating speed rounds hours down
snippets.bug: A pile that is not an exact multiple of the speed still needs one extra hour, but floor division drops it, so feasible() accepts speeds that are too slow.
snippets.explanation: Hours per pile are ceil(pile / speed), written in integers as (pile + speed - 1) // speed (or math.ceil). With the right feasible(), the search is O(n log max(piles)) time, O(1) space.

snippets.title: Heap of tasks cannot compare them
snippets.bug: heapq orders items with `<`, but Task defines no __lt__, so the second push raises TypeError ('<' not supported between instances of 'Task' and 'Task').
snippets.actual: ERROR: TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'Task' and 'Task'
snippets.explanation: Give the class an ordering (or push (priority, counter, task) tuples). Each push and pop is then O(log n), and the tasks come out by priority.

snippets.title: Dataclass shares one list
snippets.code:
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class Cart:
    owner: str
    items: list = []

    def add(self, item):
        self.items.append(item)
        return self


first = Cart("ann").add("pen")
second = Cart("bob")
print(first.items, second.items)
snippets.bug: A mutable default (`[]`) would be shared by every instance, so dataclass refuses it and raises ValueError when the class is created.
snippets.fixedCode:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Cart:
    owner: str
    items: list = field(default_factory=list)

    def add(self, item):
        self.items.append(item)
        return self


first = Cart("ann").add("pen")
second = Cart("bob")
print(first.items, second.items)
snippets.actual: ERROR: ValueError: mutable default <class 'list'> for field items is not allowed: use default_factory
snippets.explanation: Use `field(default_factory=list)` so each instance gets its own list; plain `= []` on a normal class attribute or default argument has the same sharing problem without the safety check.
